place: a Toyota Cressida from the eighties at the kerb

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Toyota could sell a car to anyone, except the people who bought a Mercedes.

place: the luxury cars Toyota's buyers moved to

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Its own best customers got richer, and traded up to Mercedes and BMW.

place: Toyota's head office in Toyota City

header.title: Leaping forward as a global corporation

lines: Toyota began developing a flagship car
for customers who wanted more than a Toyota
and were leaving for European luxury brands.
The project took roughly six years.
layers.phrase: for customers who wanted more than a Toyota

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So in 1984, Toyota started a secret project: a luxury car to win them back.

place: a test car's dashboard on a long winter road

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Its engineers drove test cars more than 3.5M kilometres.

place: a Toyota badge on a grille

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Jalopnik puts the bill at about $1B. So would a Mercedes buyer ever pay that kind of money for a Toyota?

place: the first Lexus on a showroom print

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Toyota left its own name off. Six years on, it opened Lexus in America, at $35,000 a car.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: By the end of that year, Lexus had hit its forecast of 16,000 cars.

place: the poster over the first Lexus

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Behind that one car, Toyota had built about 450 prototypes, before anyone had heard the name Lexus.

place: the Toyota from the first frame

moments.what: back to the Toyota from the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Lexus or Mercedes: which badge would you park outside? Either way, the Lexus was built by Toyota.
